newsitem.title: SYRIA: Italy's Prodi in talks with Assad in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi in talks with Assad in Syria.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi opened talks in Damascus on Sunday with President Hafez al-Assad on Syria's stalled peace talks with Israel and ways of boosting bilateral economic cooperation, officials said.

Presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam, Prime Minister Mahmoud Zu'bi and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara were present at the meeting in the presidential palace.
An official accompanying the Italian prime minister said Prodi would stress during the talks the importance of reviving the Syrian-Israeli peace talks that broke off a year ago.
He said Prodi would also reiterate Italy's position that the peace talks be based on U.N. Security Council resolutions 242 and 338, which call for the exchange of land for peace.
Syrian officials said Italy's ties with Damascus were good and were progressing.
They referred to a recent visit by Khaddam and Shara to Rome in which they explained Damascus' views regarding the resumption of peace talks with Israel.
"The Italian officials showed understanding of Syria's position regarding the peace process and stressed the importance of achieving durable peace in the Middle East," one official said.

Khaddam and Shara toured several European capitals to tell their leaders that Damascus was ready to resume peace talks with Israel from the point at which they left off with Israel's previous Labour-led government.
Syria said the previous Israeli government agreed during the talks to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.

Israel's current prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who defeated the Labour government in elections in May, said he would not pull back from the Golan and has urged Syria to resume talks without conditions.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but the negotiations were blocked over the fate of the Golan.
Italian officials said that Prodi, who is heading a 30-member economic delegation, would discuss how to boost the volume of trade between Syria and Italy.

They said that Syria's exports to Italy, which are mainly crude oil, totalled $590 million in 1995 while Italy's exports to Syria during the same year stood at $489 million. Final figures for 1996 were not available.
Syria's exports to Italy include also leather, cotton and ready-made clothes, while Italy's exports are mainly machinery and other manufactured goods.

Officials said members of Prodi's team held separate talks in Damascus on Sunday with Syria's Economy and Foreign Trade Minister Mohammed Imadi on the possibility of signing an economic cooperation agreement between the two countries.
They said the talks also covered debts that Syria should pay to Italian companies, about $25 million.
